exposure: bleeding issues (placenta previa, placental abruption, uterine bleeding, excessive bleeding, blood transfusion, unplanned hysterectomy)
cohort: A population-based cohort of 1,126,058 naturally conceived singleton live births, excluding those with chromosomal defects, born between 2004 and 2018 in New York, Texas, Massachusetts, and North Carolina.
finding: Pre-gestational diabetes and placental or bleeding issues were the strongest risk factors associated with major non-chromosomal birth defects, with hypertension, prior caesarean delivery, older maternal age, and higher pre-pregnancy BMI also being significant risk factors.
mod_finding: Prior caesarean delivery was identified as a significant risk factor for major non-chromosomal birth defects.
